validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE check. Sabal Trail Phase II is a real, well-documented compressor-only capacity expansion of the in-service Sabal Trail interstate gas transmission pipeline (FERC docket CP15-17, same docket as Phase I/P0249), confirmed independently via: EIA 'Today in Energy' (govt, Aug 24 2020, states '...the second phases of the Sabal Trail Pipeline (0.17 Bcf/d)...entered service in April [2020]'); Duke Energy's FY2020 10-K (SEC filing, independent JV-partner disclosure, 7.5% owner: 'Phase II of Sabal Trail went into service in May 2020, adding approximately 200,000 Dth of capacity'); Enbridge's FY2020 10-K (SEC filing, operator/50% owner: 'Sabal Trail Phase II - an expansion of our existing Sabal Trail pipeline through the addition of two new greenfield compressor stations in Albany, Georgia and Dunnellon, Florida'); and FERC's own Jan 2019 NTP letter + Apr 2020 in-service-authorization letter (both reproduced verbatim by the independent nonprofit WWALS Watershed Coalition, an unaffiliated opponent of the pipeline with no incentive to overstate the project's existence). Correctly classified as an interstate natural gas transmission pipeline expansion (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) -- not gathering/processing. Confirmed by three independent origins agreeing Phase II is in service since 2020: EIA (govt) states the Phase II capacity 'entered service in April' 2020; FERC's own April 22, 2020 letter order (reproduced by WWALS, an independent nonprofit) grants Sabal Trail's request 'to place into service the Sabal Trail Project Phase II Facilities, specifically the Albany and Dunnellon Compressor Stations'; Duke Energy's FY2020 10-K (independent SEC filer, 7.5% owner) states 'Phase II of Sabal Trail went into service in May 2020'. validity.recommendation: verify Capacity/CapacityUnits against the actual FERC certificate/tariff for Phase II -- EIA's 170 MMcf/d and Duke's ~200,000 Dth/d do not reconcile with a simple unit-conversion factor
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=170.00 MMcf/d for Phase II. EIA's Aug 24, 2020 'Today in Energy' article (US government, independent of the operator) states verbatim: 'the second phases of the Sabal Trail Pipeline (0.17 Bcf/d)...entered service in April', an EXACT match to GEM's 170.00 MMcf/d. However, Duke Energy's FY2020 10-K (an independent JV-partner SEC filing, not tracing to EIA or the operator) states: 'Phase II of Sabal Trail went into service in May 2020, adding approximately 200,000 Dth of capacity to the Sabal Trail pipeline.' Natural gas typically runs ~1.02-1.035 Dth per Mcf, so 170,000 Mcf/d x ~1.03 =~ 175,000 Dth/d -- notably short of Duke's stated ~200,000 Dth, a gap of roughly 14% that ordinary volumetric-vs-energy-content unit conversion does not explain. This mirrors the SAME type of Capacity discrepancy the sibling shard P0249.json flagged for Phase I (GEM 830 MMcf/d vs EIA 810 MMcf/d) -- following that shard's precedent, flagging as a spec concern rather than silently passing. Recommend the researcher pull the actual FERC order/tariff authorizing Phase II's specific incremental capacity to resolve which figure (170 MMcf/d or a Dth-derived ~194,000-196,000 Mcf/d) is the correct certificated design capacity.
